The official term should be "course section" for the enrolled class tied to NJIT records.
When a section assignment change becomes effective, calendar entries and reminders from the old section shall no longer be shown.
If a student is enrolled in multiple sections, the system shall show all applicable calendar entries and reminders.
When a student is enrolled in multiple sections, the system shall make it obvious which section each calendar entry or reminder belongs to so the student can distinguish them.
Already sent reminders should not be erased from the user’s history.
Upcoming reminders should be updated in place if the change is known early enough.
A short grace period may be allowed during the transition if needed for sync delays.
The system shall separate course-wide items from section-specific and subgroup-specific items.
Each post or file shall include a clear label indicating who it applies to.

The system shall provide a single priority or important flag for urgent updates.
Messaging should feel near real time during normal use.

Activity participation should count as recorded as soon as the system confirms the submission or action was received successfully.
Slower loads are acceptable for large files, rich media, or first-time access when the system has to initialize everything.
In normal day-to-day use, the course space should still feel responsive.
If content cannot load all at once, it should appear progressively.
When the network is weak, the system should show partial content and a clear loading state rather than a blank screen.

Content posted in a section or group shall become visible to the whole course if the instructor sets it as an announcement that everyone needs to see.
Private messages between individuals shall remain private unless there is an explicit reason to forward or copy them.
Instructors shall be able to post course content in their own sections.
Administrators shall have override access to post, edit, or remove course content when there is a support or policy reason.
Students shall usually be able to create and edit only their own contributions.

The instructor shall control whether group members are allowed limited editing rights in a group space.
Administrators shall only view user data that they need for their job.
Sensitive user data shall be restricted by role.
Access to sensitive user data shall be logged for audit purposes.
Administrators shall be allowed to intervene in an account or override access for support, security, or policy enforcement purposes.
Changing user roles or deactivating an account should require approval or at least a second review in special cases.
Special-case approval or second review is especially required when changing roles or deactivating an account affects faculty accounts or an active student record.
For user accounts, the system shall automatically merge duplicates only when the match is very strong.
For user accounts, a very strong match includes the same institutional ID or a verified email plus matching name and status.
If there is any conflict in identity details, role, or enrollment history for user accounts, the system shall send the record to manual review instead of guessing.
The system shall exclude course enrollments from automatic merge unless the course code, term, and user identity all line up cleanly.
The system shall avoid bad course-enrollment merges because they could place someone in the wrong class or hide a real enrollment.
Course records shall be kept for a period of time after the course ends.
Faculty and administration shall be able to access course records for audits, grade disputes, and accreditation purposes.
The exact retention period for course records must be confirmed with NJIT policy.
One-off access exceptions shall be allowed only in exceptional cases.
Before granting a one-off access exception, the system shall require documented approval from an appropriate supervisor or system owner.
Before granting a one-off access exception, the system shall require a time limit.
Before granting a one-off access exception, the system shall require confirmation of exactly which data or function the person can access.
One-off access exceptions shall be fully logged.
Notifications should be sent first to the people who need to respond first.
Initial notifications should keep the message minimal.
If an incident may involve privacy or legal implications, the communication should be reviewed before it is sent to the broader audience.

The log shall include any conditions attached to the access exception.

When editing or other actions are allowed under an explicitly approved exception, they should be tightly limited and logged.
The initial notice shall state that there is an incident.
The initial notice shall identify what part of the portal or course access is affected.
The initial notice shall describe who is impacted in general terms.
The initial notice shall state what immediate steps people should take.
The initial notice shall withhold detailed student information.
The initial notice shall withhold technical root-cause speculation.
The initial notice shall withhold any information that has not gone through privacy or legal review.
Later updates shall include withheld details once the situation is confirmed and cleared for release.

The first message shall not include anything that could be misleading before the issue is fully reviewed.
